title: React Architecture Applied Check
description: Apply React architecture decisions to realistic project structure, state ownership, pattern, and error-boundary scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A team adds every reusable-looking component to `shared/components` on day one. What is the likely long-term issue?

options.text: Shared code becomes a dumping ground with unclear ownership
React will stop rendering shared components
The code cannot be code split
Components cannot accept props

questions.explanation: The lessons warn that shared folders need clear ownership and should not become a default destination for uncertain code.

questions.prompt: Feature A imports `../featureB/internal/useFeatureBForm` because it is convenient. What is the architectural risk?

options.text: The import boundary is bypassed, coupling Feature A to Feature B internals
The hook will run twice automatically
The browser cannot resolve relative imports
The code becomes more accessible

questions.explanation: Feature public APIs protect ownership boundaries; reaching into internals makes later changes harder.

questions.prompt: A product page stores `selectedVariantId` and also stores a copied `selectedVariant` object that can get out of sync. What is the better approach?

options.text: Keep both and manually sync them in every handler
Store the source of truth and derive the rest when rendering
Move both values into localStorage
Put both values in separate contexts

questions.explanation: Avoid duplicated state when one value can be derived from another source of truth.

questions.prompt: Server data is cached in a broad React context and manually refetched from many screens. Which lesson principle is being missed?

options.text: Server state has different needs from local UI state
Context cannot contain arrays
Reducers are only for forms
URL state should hold API responses

questions.explanation: Server state needs cache, freshness, loading, and error handling behavior that differs from simple UI state.

questions.prompt: An error boundary fallback remains visible after the user navigates to a different item id. What is a common reset strategy?

options.text: Give the boundary a key tied to the item or route segment
Wrap the event handler in useMemo
Remove the fallback UI
Store the error in CSS

questions.explanation: Changing a boundary key remounts it, which is a common way to reset boundary state for a new route or entity.

questions.prompt: A click handler throws while saving a form, but the nearest error boundary does not catch it. What should the app do instead?

options.text: Handle the async or event error in the action flow and show explicit UI state
Move the button outside React
Convert the handler to a class method only
Disable logging

questions.explanation: Error boundaries do not catch event handler or async failures; those need ordinary error handling in the interaction flow.

questions.prompt: Which choices fit a compound component API for a reusable Modal? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Modal.Root coordinates open state
Modal.Title provides a semantic title slot
Every consumer must manually query DOM nodes
Modal.Close can access close behavior through context

questions.explanation: Compound components expose related pieces while hiding coordination details inside the parent API.

questions.prompt: A developer moves every keystroke of every input into Redux because the app is growing. What is the best critique?

options.text: Growth alone does not mean every local value belongs in global state
Redux cannot store strings
React forms must never use state
Global state always improves performance

questions.explanation: Scalable state architecture depends on ownership and sharing needs, not project size alone.
